summary: The curated contracts and implementations are broadly consistent and fail-closed, with strong artifact, credential, execution, and verification boundaries. Three bounded defects remain: UTF-8 framing uses character rather than byte lengths, foreign-framework Cypress-named files can enter Cypress scope, and the opt-in ESLint download leaves plugin versions floating.

findings.title: UTF-8 frame length uses character count
findings.evidence: The documented frame function writes ${#value} as the length, while the receiving helpers interpret that length as UTF-8 bytes. Non-ASCII URLs therefore produce incomplete or trailing-frame errors despite being accepted by the URL contract.
findings.recommendation: Compute and emit the UTF-8 byte length, and use the same framing helper for preflight and raw-ARIA requests.

findings.title: Cypress basename bypasses foreign-framework exclusion
findings.evidence: file_in_cypress_scope returns true solely for a *.cy.* basename without first applying the documented foreign-framework override. Cypress-specific mechanical rules can therefore classify a foreign-framework file as Cypress scope based on its name alone.
findings.recommendation: Apply the foreign-test-module exclusion before basename admission unless executable Cypress provenance is also present.

findings.title: Opt-in ESLint plugins are not version-bounded
findings.evidence: The legacy download command pins eslint to ^9 but requests eslint-plugin-$plugin and the parser without explicit versions. Enabling downloads can consequently execute changing latest plugin/parser releases, contrary to the stated deliberate dependency boundary.
findings.recommendation: Pin explicit reviewed versions for every downloaded package and update them only through a deliberate release change.

limitations: Packet-only static review; no commands, tests, scanners, benchmarks, holdouts, network checks, or runtime probes were executed.
The curated subset omits referenced helpers, tests, manifests, agent files, and CI dependencies, so their behavior and completeness cannot be assessed.
This is not full product coverage, skill-accuracy evidence, independent ground truth, human or sealed review, or remote model attestation.
